description:
docs/beam-nifs.md (defk-7w2, 2026-10-06) anchors its claims to `file:line` references that have drifted since the credo/dialyzer refactors (defk-x15, 2026-10-09). Checked 2026-10-09:
- "`lib/defk/compiler.ex:1925`" and ":1908" for the two enif_schedule_nif calls: now lines 2467 and 2437.
- "the safepoint macro is `lib/defk/compiler.ex:1870`": now 2405.
- "`priv/defk_runtime.h:395-397`" for DEFK_SLICE_US: now 425. "409-430" for defk_tick: now 443 onwards.
- The remaining ~15 references (defk_bind, defk_promote, defk_raise, defk_finish, the allocation table rows, guard_fn lines) are off by similar amounts.

Fix: replace each `file:line` with the symbol it points at (`defk_tick` in priv/defk_runtime.h, `sp_macro/2` in lib/defk/compiler.ex, `step_fn/3`, ...) so the document does not rot with every refactor; where a line range genuinely helps, keep it as "around `symbol`". Add a short note at the top saying references are by symbol name. Optionally a test or `mix ci` step that greps the doc for `\.(ex|h):\d+` and fails if any remain.

Done when: the document has no `file:line` references, every named symbol exists (grep), and `mix ci` is green.
title: docs/beam-nifs.md cites stale line numbers; reference symbols instead
